summary: Children, parents and a spouse have a protected share that a will cannot override (Civil Code arts. 505-506). A foreigner's estate follows their national law, except Turkish real estate, which follows Turkish law. Turkey has no trust law and family foundations are not allowed, and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
reserved_share: Descendants: one half of their statutory share; each parent: one quarter of theirs; the spouse: all of the statutory share when with descendants or parents, otherwise three quarters (Civil Code art. 506). Siblings' share was repealed in 2007. Free portion is the rest (art. 505).
foreign_law_note: Law No. 5718 on Private International Law art. 20: succession follows the deceased's national law; immovables in Turkey follow Turkish law. A foreigner therefore keeps national law for movables only. Turkish courts may use public policy.
trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. Turkey has no trust law and does not clearly recognise a foreign trust. Foundations (vakif) are under Civil Code arts. 101-117 and the Foundations Law; the Code does not allow a foundation whose purpose is to support the founder's family. Foreign foundations are regulated separately.
open_questions: Confirm Law 5718 art. 20 text and the Foundations Law wording on family foundations (art. 101); I relied on knowledge.
Confirm how Turkish tax treats distributions from foreign trusts.
